procedures_covered: External intermittent cardiac event monitors / AEMs
Mobile cardiac outpatient telemetry (not medically necessary)

logic.top_level: pathways (I external any-of; III ILR with three sub-pathways, each all-of)
logic.exclusions_or_contraindications: II and V investigational lists; IV MCOT not medically necessary; Guideline II convenience items ineligible; external monitor 'contraindicated (i.e., severe skin conditions or obesity)' as substitute for the 28-day failed trial.
logic.initial_vs_repeat: Repeat studies within one year are 'subject to medical necessity review'; ILR or battery replacement needs malfunction and expired warranty and documentation it 'will significantly change the plan of care'.

and_or_ambiguity.quote: Documentation supporting that the continuation of an ILR or battery replacement will significantly change the plan of care; a, or
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: Guideline III A-D joined by 'and' ... 'a, or' (stray text) before D 'irreparable changes...'; whether D is an alternative is unclear

and_or_ambiguity.quote: Failure of a 28-day external cardiac event monitor to establish a definitive diagnosis; or when an external cardiac event monitor is contraindicated
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: The 'or' sits inside an item of an ALL-of list

requirement_kinds.quote: To assess signs or symptoms possibly related to rhythm disturbances (e.g., palpitations, serious or significant syncope, near syncope)
After an ablation procedure to assess the results for residual arrhythmias
After initiation of anti-arrhythmic drug therapy to assess the effectiveness
Failure of a 28-day external cardiac event monitor to establish a definitive diagnosis
Documentation supporting that an ILR will significantly change the plan of care
Received a thorough stroke evaluation by a neurologist or qualified provider from a certified stroke center
48-72 hours of electrocardiogram (EKG) monitoring with failure to demonstrate an arrhythmia

at a minimum, CT or MRI of brain, arterial imaging, CTA, MRA or ultrasound of carotid circulation, echocardiography, extended rhythm monitoring, and key laboratory studies such as a lipid profile and hemoglobin A1c
repeat studies within one (1) year of a previous study are subject to medical necessity review

time_windows.quote: within one (1) year of a previous study
